title: Slope-screened acreage at 3 feet, 30 feet, and 1/3 arc-second in Stayton, Oregon

method.county_boundary: Densify WGS84 boundary segments to at most 0.00003 degrees before transformation. Transform from WGS84 to the native grid CRS.
method.slope: Horn 3 × 3. The east–west gradient is ((NE + 2E + SE) − (NW + 2W + SW)) / (8 × dx). The north–south gradient is ((NW + 2N + NE) − (SW + 2S + SE)) / (8 × dy). Slope percent is 100 times the Euclidean magnitude of the two gradients.
method.spacing: Use matching units within each calculation. For the USGS geographic cells, calculate row-specific centre-latitude east–west and north–south cell spacing geodesically in metres on GRS80. The Oregon grid uses international feet for both spacing and elevation.
method.controlled_downsample: Average complete non-overlapping 10 × 10 blocks aligned to the 3-foot window, then compute slope. The 30-foot grid is an analytical control.
method.edge_handling: Compute the slopes on buffered input windows before clipping. Retain only cells with a complete 3 × 3 neighbourhood. There is valid slope coverage for the entire lot.
method.area: Intersect each native-grid cell with the densified parcel. Undo the parcel-to-grid transform before projecting intersections to EPSG:5070 and summing areas in acres. Use a fractional weight for boundary cells.
method.connected_area: Label eligible cells that share an edge, with a positive intersection area inside the parcel. Sum the eligible cell fraction weights within each group and retain the largest. This is a raster sensitivity check.
method.scope: The thresholds are examples for a desktop screen. The source grids and aerial photos have different vintages. This comparison does not estimate changes in ground height or establish an engineered development footprint.

elevation_window.encoding: base64 of zlib-compressed row-major float bytes

dogami_30ft_mean.derived_window_instruction: Average non-overlapping 10 by 10 blocks from the complete dogami_3ft window, in row-major order. Every input cell was valid.
